title: Local distinguishability of five quadripartite orthogonal product states
authors: Guang-Bao Xu, Jie Zhan, Yu-Guang Yang, Dong-Huan Jiang
abstract: The local distinguishability of five bipartite and tripartite orthogonal product states (OPSs) has been effectively resolved, while that of five quadripartite OPSs has not yet been effectively addressed. In this paper, we give the local distinguishability of five quadripartite OPSs, where any two of these five states are orthogonal on exactly one subsystem. Based on the vectors of the numbers of pairwise orthogonality relations, we classify different sets of five quadripartite OPSs into nine categories, which correspond to 371 distinct orthogonality graphs. We show that the sets of five quadripartite OPSs corresponding to 355 of the 371 cases can be perfectly distinguished by local operations and classical communication (LOCC), whereas the sets of five quadripartite OPSs for the remaining 16 cases cannot exactly distinguished by LOCC. Our results enrich the theory of nonlocality for sets of OPSs.
summary: This theoretical paper investigates the local distinguishability of five specific quadripartite orthogonal product states. By classifying the states based on their pairwise orthogonality patterns, the authors determine that most configurations (355 out of 371) can be perfectly distinguished using LOCC. This enriches the understanding of nonlocality in multipartite quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper determines the local distinguishability of sets of five quadripartite orthogonal product states (OPSs).
main_result: The sets corresponding to 355 out of 371 possible orthogonality graphs can be perfectly distinguished by LOCC, while 16 specific cases cannot.
method: The analysis involves classifying the states based on the vector of pairwise orthogonality relations and applying theorems (like Theorem 1 and Theorem 2) derived from local measurements to test for perfect distinguishability.
model_or_system: The system consists of five quadripartite orthogonal product states $|\psi_iangle = |\alpha_iangle_1 | eta_iangle_2 |\gamma_iangle_3 |\delta_iangle_4$ in a four-partite Hilbert space.
key_observables: The vector of the numbers of pairwise orthogonality relations, and the degree of a vertex in the associated orthogonality graph.
important_parameters: The structure of the orthogonality graph, characterized by the colors of the edges corresponding to the four subsystems.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on established results for bipartite and tripartite OPSs, and assumes that equivalent graphs obtained by permutations are omitted.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate feasible orthogonality graphs for specific categories, such as those related to (2, 2, 2) or (7, 1, 1, 1), detailing the structural analysis.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the classification of five OPSs using the orthogonality graph structure, applying theorems to prove distinguishability for most cases and identifying 16 exceptional cases where LOCC fails.
why_interesting: It deepens the theory of nonlocality for sets of OPSs by providing a comprehensive classification of when such states can be perfectly distinguished using only local measurements and classical communication.
